awarding_org: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien)
funder_origin_name: Rolf Schock bequest / Rolf Schock Foundation (Schockstiftelsen)
funding_share_basis: 100% of the purse comes from the estate of philosopher and artist Rolf Schock (d. 1986), who willed half his fortune to fund four prizes; the ring-fenced Rolf Schock Foundation, formed 1987-88, has invested and paid out that endowment ever since, so the single funder exceeds 50% in both the origin and current states. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences selects and confers the mathematics laureate but contributes no money.
money_note: The 2026 purse is SEK 600,000 per prize area (SEK 2.4 million across the four prizes), paid from the Schock Foundation's management of the Schock bequest; the mathematics prize has been awarded since 1993 and is currently given every second year (2024, 2026).
evidence_quote: Upon his death in 1986, Rolf Schock left behind a considerable fortune. In his will, he stipulated that half of his estate should be used to fund four prizes... The Schock Foundation administers the donated funds.
judgment_reason: KVA states that the Schock Foundation 'formally decides the laureates' while the Academy reviews and proposes them, so a coder could name the Rolf Schock Foundation (Philanthropy) as the awarding organization. I coded the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences because it runs the selection committee, announces the mathematics laureate, and confers the prize, with the foundation acting as the financial trustee.
